candidate.title: OS-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle row labeled OS-Seq (oligonucleotide-selective sequencing): a genomic single-adapter library and an independently modified flow-cell primer lawn converge for target hybridization, primer-extension capture, bridge formation, template completion and paired-end sequencing. The 2011 Myllykangas implementation resolves surface-primer and read identities. The Gene/Target sequence drawings specify the biological target and probe design, not an additional excision workflow. TSCS above and Safe-SeqS below are neighboring rows, not alternatives or branches of OS-Seq. No later automation, clinical panel, sample indexing or additional assay version is extracted.

operations.label: Create target-specific oligos
operations.description: Introduce target-specific oligonucleotide templates to the original flow-cell primer lawn and anneal their universal segment to its complementary surface primer. The depicted product is the template–surface-primer hybrid before extension.

operations.label: Extend and Denature

operations.label: Extend and Denature

method_scopes.rationale: OS-Seq is the sole assigned target and the expanded oligonucleotide-selective sequencing name is its alias. All eight local operations belong to the middle row; repeated Hybridize and Extend and Denature captions refer to distinct transformations of different material states. The primary 2011 paper supports the depicted single-adapter/modified-primer-lawn implementation. Other OS-Seq papers are related evidence, without establishing that every later implementation uses identical preparation.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection covers all 11 states, eight local operations, 18 flows, OS-Seq applicability and five paper assessments. Both preparation branches converge at target hybridization. The three extension/denaturation instances and two hybridization instances retain distinct substrates and support attachment; downstream interfaces preserve the copied target, distal adapter tail and synthetic probe association. Each multi-input operation is a genuine joint complex formation; the final bridge extension acts jointly on one bridged complex. Every in-scope depicted transformation is represented. Primary-text clarification of C/D primer identities, released versus retained strands, and reads 1/2 agrees with the schematic, so no consequential correction or blocking unknown remains. This review is bound to the canonical candidate digest supplied in the caller context.
